nodes.label: ValidatedTransaction verifies the signed transaction hash against its transaction public key; this establishes signature validity, not a proof of user outcome constraints.
Ordinary access-key verification checks nonce, available balance, allowance, storage stake and function-call permission before returning the charged account amount and updated nonce.
Function-call permission requires exactly one FunctionCall, zero attached NEAR, matching receiver and an allowed method if the list is nonempty.
Accepted transactions create an ActionReceipt and SuccessReceiptId; signer-equal receivers enter a local queue, others go through forwarding or buffering.
Transaction account/key state is applied and committed independently before later receipt success or failure.
The VM runner validates/prepares/instruments/links contract code and runs the configured backend; guest aborts and gas must be deterministic across validators.
Function-call execution collects burnt/used gas and logs even on abort; successful execution exports newly created receipts and updates account balance/storage.
Runtime storage keys bind ContractData to current account; writes are prospective TrieUpdate entries while reads record witness paths.
TrieUpdate rollback clears prospective writes and pending deployments, not already committed changes.
Gas accounting distinguishes burnt gas and reserved promise gas and rejects hard-limit, prepaid-limit or arithmetic overflow violations.
Pinned source constants are stable 88, minimum supported 84, nightly157 and Spice binary200; Spice activates at180. These constants alone do not establish live network activation.
GasKeys source activation is85 while the pinned access-key docs say86; this is an unresolved source/docs discrepancy.
Pinned lifecycle docs say refunds always succeed, but runtime explicitly handles system-refund failure by burning the deposit; do not use the documentation blanket statement as a theorem.
Final execution status follows SuccessReceiptId links, so first-receipt-only prose is incomplete; side branches are not necessarily the status-determining branch.
VM context distinguishes original signer, immediate predecessor, refund recipient, account state, attached deposit, prepaid gas and promise results.

A failed action batch clears all its newly queued receipts, proposals and receipt token adjustments, retaining gas, logs and profile; actions stop at the first failure. Prospective action writes roll back, but dependency consumption was already committed and a receiver gas reward can commit afterward.

promise_and flattens receipt dependencies into a non-receipt promise. then creates a receipt with these dependencies. The runtime waits for data availability, including explicit failed results, not unanimous success.

Ordinary generated action receipts preserve original signer and key, assign the current contract as predecessor, and carry deposit/gas/refund context; they do not constitute freshly signed access-key transactions. Contract-level continuation authorization remains necessary.

Failed action deposits become balance-refund receipts; gas refund uses burnt gas on failure and used gas on success, subtracts a penalty, and depends on protocol price/account-creation rules. Deposit and gas refunds can have different recipients.

A postponed receipt and its pending dependency count persist in trie state. Callback failure does not establish a fresh retry receipt; a durable application duty and permitted retry/recovery transition must be specified separately.

NEP-509 describes trie inclusion evidence permitting state-transition replay and signed chunk endorsements; ZK integration is explicitly out of scope. Neither transaction signatures nor replay alone proves refinement of signed economic intent.

The inspected actor-permission function admits ordinary function calls without account-owner equality; owner equality is required for deployment and key management. Permissionless deployment does not imply unrestricted modification of another account.

Callback panic rolls back its own cleanup and transfer scheduling. The docs example is imprecise when saying the transfer line never runs: a transfer may have been queued before panic but its receipt is discarded.

edges.rationale: Signature validation is an earlier transaction phase.
Transaction charging survives receipt action rollback.
The join becomes a receipt waiting for data.
Action rollback and protocol refunds are distinct.
Returned status path differs from dependency result vector.
State replay and signatures do not establish formal-intent refinement.
